summary: The Philippines admits citizens of more than 150 countries visa-free for 30 days — extendable by 29 days at a Bureau of Immigration office — and requires every arriving traveler to register on the free eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival. Airlines strictly check onward tickets before boarding.

ZW.notes: Visa-free for 30 days under Executive Order 408; extendable by 29 days (visa waiver) at a Bureau of Immigration office, and further in-country extensions are routine.

conditionalWaivers.text: Indian citizens holding a valid US, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or UK visa or residence permit may enter the Philippines visa-free for 30 days for tourism (not extendable).

fee.notes: Embassy in Washington, for nationals who need a visa: USD 40 single entry valid three months, USD 80 multiple entry for six months, USD 120 for one year (nationals of visa-free countries pay USD 30, 60 and 90; Chinese nationals USD 25, 50 and 100). Other missions charge the equivalent in local currency. e-Visa applications add a USD 25 convenience fee.

fee.notes: The eVisa is currently offered only to selected nationalities (rolled out first for Chinese nationals, with Indian nationals announced). Fees mirror the 9a visa and vary by class. Check evisa.gov.ph for eligibility and the current fee.

fee.notes: PHP 500 visa waiver fee, PHP 1,000 application fee, PHP 500 certification fee, PHP 30 legal research fee and PHP 1,000 express fee, paid at a Bureau of Immigration office (the BI dates this table 6 March 2014). Further monthly extensions are possible afterward, up to 36 months in total for visa-free nationals.

vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Bureau of Immigration / Bureau of Quarantine entry rules

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement for tourists, but medical coverage is strongly recommended — private hospitals expect payment or proof of insurance up front.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free entry legally requires an onward or return ticket, and airlines enforce this strictly at check-in — travelers without one are routinely denied boarding.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published, but immigration officers may ask about means of support and accommodation for the stay.

declarations.name: eTravel Registration
declarations.text: Every traveler arriving in the Philippines (foreigners and Filipinos alike) must register on the eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival and present the QR code at check-in and immigration. It is completely free. Use only etravel.gov.ph.

source.name: eTravel — Frequently Asked Questions

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over 10,000 USD (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure. Bringing in or taking out more than 50,000 PHP in Philippine currency requires prior authorization from the central bank (BSP).

source.name: Bureau of Customs — e-Travel customs declaration and BSP rules on bringing in or taking out currencies

notes: Duty-free allowance: 2 cartons of cigarettes and 2 bottles of alcohol (up to 1 liter each) per adult.
The customs declaration is completed electronically as part of eTravel registration.

payments.text: Cards work in city hotels, malls and chain restaurants, but jeepneys, tricycles, markets, small eateries and most of the islands run on cash. GCash QR payments are everywhere locally but need a Philippine SIM and account.

safety.text: Most tourist areas of the Philippines are generally safe with normal precautions, though petty theft occurs in cities. Western governments advise against travel to parts of Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago due to terrorism and kidnapping risk.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Philippines travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to May is the dry season across most of the archipelago — December to February is coolest, March to May hottest. June to November brings rain and typhoons.

tips.text: Book an onward or return ticket before you fly — Philippine carriers and foreign airlines alike will refuse boarding without one for visa-free travelers.
eTravel registration is free. Third-party sites charging a fee for the QR code are scams. Use only etravel.gov.ph.
Long stays are easy: after the initial 30 days you can keep extending at Bureau of Immigration offices (first a 29-day visa waiver, then 1–6 month extensions), for years in total.
Typhoon season runs roughly June to November — ferries and domestic flights get canceled at short notice, so build slack into island-hopping plans.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 30 days with a passport valid 6 months and an onward ticket. The stay can be extended by 29 days (and beyond) at Bureau of Immigration offices. Everyone must also register on eTravel within 72 hours before arrival.

faq.question: What is eTravel and who needs it?
faq.answer: eTravel (etravel.gov.ph) is the Philippines' free online arrival registration combining immigration, health and customs declarations. Every arriving traveler — foreign or Filipino — must complete it within 72 hours before arrival and show the QR code at check-in and on arrival.

faq.question: Is an onward ticket really required for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Yes. Proof of onward or return travel is a legal condition of visa-free entry, and airlines check it rigorously at check-in — passengers without it are routinely denied boarding. A cheap real ticket to any other country satisfies the rule.

faq.question: How do I extend my stay in the Philippines?
faq.answer: Apply at any Bureau of Immigration office (or the BI e-services portal) before your current stay expires. The first step is a 29-day visa waiver (PHP 3,030); after that you can extend in 1, 2 or 6-month increments, generally up to 36 months total for visa-free nationals.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Indian passport holders with a valid visa or residence permit for the US, UK, Schengen area, Japan, Australia, Canada or Singapore can enter visa-free for 14 days (extendable by 7). Without one, they need a temporary visitor (9a) visa. An eVisa route for Indian nationals has also been announced. Confirm current rules with the Bureau of Immigration before booking.
